title: An 11-Day-Old Baby Couldn’t Stop Bleeding. For Hours, the ER Didn’t Provide a Critical Vitamin Shot.
content:
The emergency room was a mile from their Texas home. Stephanie and Eric Biesenbach took comfort in that when their newborn daughter, Gwen, wouldn’t stop bleeding from her belly button. They buckled Gwen into her car seat and made the drive over. 

Medical records from that warm August evening in 2023 described her condition as a “generic problem” of a bleeding umbilical cord stump. The doctor on duty, Nicole Malouf, had treated plenty of those as an emergency room specialist. She covered Gwen’s oozing belly button with a special gauze to stanch the flow, and when it appeared to stop, she sent Stephanie, Eric and Gwen on their way. 

They made it as far as the parking lot before they noticed Gwen had bled through her footed pajamas. Eric slid his arm under the car seat handle and lifted his 11-day-old daughter out of the car. They walked back toward the glaring lights of the Lonestar 24HR ER, a freestanding emergency department in New Braunfels next to a car wash, a McDonald’s and a deli.

title: Beyond the beaches: The Dominican Republic and the global debate over deep-sea mining
content:
The challenge is not solely to declare new protected areas, but ensure they have effective management

Originally published on Global Voices

The stunning beauty of the Dominican Republic’s north coast at Los Haitises National Park. Photo by Jason Boldero on Flickr (CC BY 2.0).

When you think of the Dominican Republic, the first thing that might come to mind is paradise where sun, sand, and sea combine to offer unforgettable experiences to Dominican families and global travellers alike — but the country’s deep sea is also of critical importance.

Jonathan Delance, director of conservation of the National 30×30 Program of the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources, says that Dominican marine ecosystems are one of the country’s “greatest natural and strategic riches” — diverse, highly connected, and fundamental to national life.

From an ecological standpoint, coral reefs, mangroves, seagrass beds, dunes, beaches, pelagic zones, and deep-sea ecosystems sustain biodiversity. From an economic and social standpoint, they are the foundation of tourism, fishing, and coastal protection.

title: Yes, the COP climate talks are far from perfect. But they still hold the power for change
content:
This week, around 80 world leaders – including Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese – will descend on the coastal Turkish city of Antalya for the annual United Nations climate summit, COP31. For the first time, the summit duties will be shared; Turkey will play host, while Australia leads negotiations.

At home, these national leaders have no shortage of issues to contend with: the challenges of AI, major wars and declining trust in democracy. Yet looming over all of them is the existential threat posed by a heating planet.

Climate change is a truly global challenge. Greenhouse gases have no respect for national boundaries, and the devastating impacts are being felt everywhere. We don’t have a world government, but we do have processes of international diplomacy to hammer out shared commitments. This is how the world is trying to deal with the climate crisis.

It can be easy to be pessimistic, but COP31 can still deliver real progress. In Antalya, countries will consider a global electrification target to hasten the shift from coal, oil and gas toward clean electricity.

If agreement can be found, this will be a major step forward.

title: COP31: World leaders must break fossil fuels’ grip on climate policy and people’s futures.
content:
World leaders at COP31 in Türkiye must stop backing the fossil fuel industry and start delivering the rapid, equitable phase-out that science, human rights and international law demand, Amnesty International said today.

“The world is not running out of climate warnings. It is running out of excuses. After more than 30 years of climate negotiations, governments can no longer hide behind promises of future action or avoid confronting their fossil fuel industry allies. The climate crisis is not a failure of knowledge, but a failure of political courage. It is time to break the stranglehold of corporate power over political decision-making and end the fossil fuel era before it ends us,” said Marta Schaaf, Programme Director for Climate, ESJ and Corporate Accountability at Amnesty International.

The climate crisis is not a failure of knowledge, but a failure of political courage.

Marta Schaaf, Programme Director for Climate, ESJ and Corporate Accountability at Amnesty International

title: The EU’s Industrial Accelerator Act and the Limits of Strategic Protection
content: The European Commission’s proposed Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA) marks a significant shift toward a more interventionist industrial policy. This Brief examines the IAA mechanisms intended to reduce Europe’s dependence on China in the battery and electric vehicle (EV) sectors (the IAA’s coverage of sectors such as cement and steel is not addressed). Although the objective of strengthening Europe’s industrial base is understandable, the proposed measures are unlikely to achieve that objective. Origin requirements and foreign investment screening are weakened by broad exemptions for free-trade partners, while thresholds based on price differentials between European and Chinese production are too low to incentivize private investment in Europe. By underestimating the scale of China’s competitive advantages and paying insufficient attention to global market conditions, the IAA risks raising prices within the EU without delivering meaningful strategic gains.

title: It is time the government treated hunger and obesity as two interlinked problems | Letter
content:
The cabinet committee the MPs want should become the delivery arm of a statutory right to adequate food, writes Prof Kent Buse of the World Obesity Federation

Your report (UK government’s obesity plan ‘doomed to fail’, MPs warn, 30 October) arrives a fortnight after the Right to Food UK Commission asked the same prime minister for the same thing: a legal duty on government, a minister responsible for it, and an independent body reporting to parliament.

Each report sees half the problem. The Health and Social Care Committee wants prevention and treatment run as separate workstreams, and stops at urging ministers to stand up to the food industry. The commission sees hunger as a question of income and rights, but says little about the quality of the diet that low incomes buy. The same food system, and the same households, produce both hunger and obesity. Whitehall treats them as two problems, with two sets of ministers and no shared accountability, and so neither is solved.
snippet: The cabinet committee the MPs want should become the delivery arm of a statutory right to adequate food, writes Prof Kent Buse of the World Obesity Federation

title: EU countries still can’t get it together on AI
content:
BRUSSELS — As European leaders prepare to project urgency at their first joint meeting on artificial intelligence, their governments are missing important AI safety and infrastructure targets.

The bloc’s 27 leaders are meeting Friday in Dublin to discuss how to accelerate efforts to stay safe and be more competitive on artificial intelligence.

Yet 16 capitals have missed a deadline to appoint a national authority to enforce the bloc’s AI safety law, and Brussels has also pushed back an effort to support the buildout of data centers because of national administrative delays.

European Parliament lawmaker Sergey Lagodinsky, a German member of the Greens, said the delays are undermining capitals’ credibility when speaking about Europe’s AI ambitions.

“Stop blaming the EU for missing the race if you miss your own deadlines,” he said. “Europe’s AI ambitions cannot be delivered if national capitals cannot get their act together.”

In a letter seen by POLITICO, Lagodinsky asked the European Commission to start a formal procedure against capitals for failing to meet their legal requirements under the AI law.

title: Tasavallan presidentti palkitsi 26 isää kunniamerkein valtakunnallisessa isänpäiväjuhlassa
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb myönsi kasvatustyössä ansioituneille isille kunniamerkin Säätytalossa järjestetyssä valtakunnallisessa isänpäiväjuhlassa sunnuntaina 8. marraskuuta 2026.

Juhlassa luovutettiin 26 isälle Suomen Valkoisen Ruusun I luokan mitali kultaristein. Kunniamerkki on tunnustus isille, jotka ovat paitsi ansioituneet lasten ja nuorten esimerkillisinä kasvattajina, ovat myös antaneet tärkeää tukeaan yhteisöjen jäsenille ja osallistuneet yhteiskunnan rakentamiseen erilaisissa luottamustehtävissä. Ehdotuksia kunniamerkin saajista lupa- ja valvontavirastolle ovat voineet tehdä kunnat, seurakunnat, yhdistykset ja muut yhteisöt sekä perheen lapset.

Useilla palkituista on biologisten lasten lisäksi myös bonuslapsia. Joukossa on muun muassa sijaisvanhempia, yksinhuoltajia sekä Suomeen muuttaneita isiä, joista osa on ollut tukemassa maahan muuttaneiden kotoutumista. Palkittavien isien keski-ikä tänä vuonna on 63 vuotta. Iäkkäin palkittu on 94-vuotias ja nuorin 42-vuotias.

Puheenvuoron juhlassa pitivät sosiaali- ja terveysministeri Wille Rydman ja Väestöliiton toimitusjohtaja Tiina Ristikari. Lisäksi Vaskivuoren lukion kuoro esitti musiikkiesityksiä.

title: How women bore the consequences of the First World War in British India
content:
Who do we forget on Remembrance Day?

For a long time, histories of the First World War have been popularly understood in a Euro-centric manner. But descendants of Indian soldiers and researchers have long pushed for recognition for the approximately 1.4 million men from current-day India, Pakistan and Bangladesh who helped wage the First World War for the British Empire.

Yet when it comes to the war’s impact on British India, many of us still think of contributions as military and masculine.

The double portrait of two Sikh risaldars, Jagat Singh and Man Singh, currently on display at the Art Gallery of Ontario is a testament to such recognition.

The men hailed from Punjab, the hub of military recruitment known as the “sword arm” of the Raj.

The piece was painted in London by Phillip de László two months before the Battle of the Somme in 1916, when many Indian soldiers were wounded or lost their lives.
snippet: Who do we forget on Remembrance Day?
creator: Umaima Miraj, PhD Candidate of Sociology with a Collaborative Specialization in Women and Gender Studies, University of Toronto

title: Standing in the way of slop bowls: the woman blocking food delivery robots
content:
Semi-retired professor Carolyn Marvin became a local celebrity facing down Philadelphia’s growing robot delivery army: ‘It’s my first amendment right to protest’

“One of you needs to be on the lookout for cops, while I block the robot, OK?”

It is a crisp fall morning in Philadelphia. Tucked away in a dingy alley, opposite a garage called Patriot Parking, 78-year-old Carolyn Marvin is laying out some ground rules for a robot-disrupting expedition. Once a suitable target is identified, we will follow it to a busy sidewalk and Marvin will stand in front of the robot, blocking its way. The photographer and I will take turns ensuring we’re not all carted off by the police.

title: Texas’ School Voucher Program Could Be “Unrecognizable, If Not Extinct,” Says Democratic Lawmaker
content:
Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s vision for education was finally coming together. 

This year, the state launched a voucher program that allowed roughly 110,000 of Texas’ more than 5 million schoolchildren to get a private education using taxpayer dollars. Abbott’s loyal appointee at the Texas Education Agency, Commissioner Mike Morath, was leading the state’s largest takeover of public schools in recent history. And the Texas State Board of Education, with Abbott’s support, helped pass a controversial new social studies curriculum that required teaching Bible stories and shifted away from world history to focus on Texas and the United States.

On Tuesday night, as Democrats clinched nearly every office in the state, it all began to unravel. 

In a speech after denying Abbott a fourth term, Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa called for a reversal of his education agenda. She pledged to fire Morath and to end the public school takeovers. 

Perhaps most significantly, she doubled down on a campaign promise to erase one of Abbott’s biggest accomplishments: school vouchers.
snippet: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s vision for education was finally coming together.

title: How people in Montenegro are making their country cleaner
content:
And helping to make the goals for EU accession plausible 

Originally published on Global Voices

Screenshot from the EkoMapa website of the EkoGard organization in Montenegro. Fair use.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement. 

Montenegro is on its way to joining the EU; at the moment, the goal is to do so by 2028. The United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) review in 2025 states that the country has made significant progress in aligning its environmental legal and regulatory framework, as well as much of its national legislation, with European Union (EU) directives. 

However, some problems remain, including waste management and a very low recycling rate —  less than 2 percent, far below the EU’s 50 percent target.
snippet:

title: ESSAY: The Illusion of Decentralization: Cryptocurrency and the Contradictions of Digital Capitalism
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 7 November 2026 (IDN) — In a sophisticated cyberattack whose most intensive phase lasted approximately twenty minutes, hackers stole an estimated $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what investigators have described as the biggest digital asset theft in history.

The attack, whose precise mechanism remains under investigation, involved multiple points of breach and allowed hackers to transfer billions of dollars in digital assets into wallets under their control. Blockchain investigators have attributed the operation with high confidence to a North Korean hacking organization, although the investigation remains ongoing. Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals, pledged to cover customer losses, and coordinated with other cryptocurrency companies to freeze approximately $2.85 billion in affected assets.

title: Paraguayan President Impeached and Arrested Amid Financial Meltdown and Mass Protests
content:
Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has been impeached and arrested amid a financial crisis that triggered mass protests, and turned his own Colorado party against him.

The crisis was sparked by a major digital bank being ordered into insolvency earlier in the week. Peña previously had shares in the holding company that owned the digital lender, Ueno Bank. Peña has denied allegations that he helped protect Ueno from scrutiny.

In addition to holding public funds, Ueno banked millions of private citizens who have now been left without access to their accounts. 

In a Thursday statement announcing his resignation, posted to Facebook, Peña said his “greatest wish” was that funds would be returned to Ueno customers. He said he was resigning in order to "bring calm to the population."

By that time, the streets of downtown Asunción, the nation's capital, were teeming with protesters. In the Chamber of Deputies, both his allies and opponents rejected Peña’s resignation, and instead proceeded with an impeachment process. 

The matter then fell to senators who held an extraordinary session on Friday. Peña did not appear in person for his defense in the Senate, though he sent his lawyer, Ricardo Preda.

title: Jaakko Mäntyjärven Four Shakespeare Songs palkittiin Vuoden kuoroteoksena
content:
Säveltäjä Jaakko Mäntyjärven Four Shakespeare Songs palkittiin vuoden 2026 Kuorogaalassa Vuoden kuoroteoksena. Teosto on Kuorogaalan yhteistyökumppani ja jakoi palkinnon gaalassa.

Vuonna 1984 sävelletty Four Shakespeare Songs on neljän sekakuoroteoksen sarja William Shakespearen teksteihin. Sarjaan kuuluvat Come Away, Death, Lullaby, Double, Double Toil and Trouble ja Full Fathom Five.

Yli 40 vuotta sitten valmistunut teos on säilyttänyt vahvan asemansa kuorojen ohjelmistossa ja sitä myydään ja esitetään laajasti ympäri maailmaa, muun muassa Yhdysvalloissa, Japanissa, Isossa-Britanniassa, Ruotsissa ja Saksassa. Kuluneen vuoden aikana teoksen ja sen osien nuotteja on myyty yli 1 900 kappaletta.

Säveltäjä Jaakko Mäntyjärvi on Suomen kansainvälisesti tunnetuimpia kuoromusiikin säveltäjiä, jonka teokset ammentavat laajasti eri tyyleistä ja aikakausista. Häneltä on julkaistu noin 150 kuoroteosta, ja hänen tuotantoaan esitetään laajasti eri puolilla maailmaa.

Kuorogaalassa julkistetaan myös neljä muuta vuoden aikana menestynyttä kuoroteosta: Mia Makaroffin Butterfly, Jaakko Mäntyjärven Canticum Calamitatis Maritimae sekä Pulchra es sekä Anna-Mari Kähärän Itken pois.

title: OPINION: From the Strait of Hormuz to the Strait of Midterm, Trump Pays Heavy Price
content:
By Azu Ishiekwene

The writer is the Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and the author of the new book Writing for Media and Monetising It.

ABUJA, Nigeria | 7 November 2026 (IDN) — Those who voted for President Donald Trump and handed the Republicans a majority in the US Congress two years ago cannot claim it was a mistake. Twenty-two years ago, Dick Stoken wrote in The Great Game of Politics that there’s a psychology that explains why we elect whom we elect.

The midterm results just re-echoed Stoken’s point that the pendulum of US politics swings toward the middle all the time, not despite the voters, but because of them.

One Trump term (2017–2021) was enough. But because the Democratic Party had lost its way by creating a nanny state, compounding red tape, and deifying wokeism, Trump’s idiosyncrasies looked like middle ground. He was voted in again in 2024, despite his hubris.

title: The datacentre arms race hits pause in south-east Asia
content:
Power and water constraints are pressuring what seemed like a juggernaut of growth for the region just months ago

In early 2026, Thailand’s datacentre industry was on a roll. The country’s board of investment had recently announced approval of datacentre projects from Tiktok, a UAE-based Skyline datacentre and Singapore’s Bridge datacentres, totalling a planned investment of $27bn.

As the year has passed, however, what once seemed like a new industrial juggernaut has ground to a halt. Thailand paused construction on 49 projects and approval decisions on 117 more in September 2026, amidst growing concern about the lack of sufficient details for regulation and monitoring. It is not alone in reconsidering datacentre projects. In neighbouring Indonesia, the governor of the country’s most populous province of West Java halted construction on a datacentre due to lack of permits and an incomplete environmental assessment process.

title: Can Congress Narrow the Transatlantic Tech Divide?
content:
European tech policy leaders are cautious.

Democrats won both chambers of Congress, many of whom campaigned on reigning in tech billionaires, curtailing energy-intensive data centers, and imposing artificial intelligence safety rules. These positions could bring US tech policy much closer to Europe’s strict approach.

But European politicians and analysts warned against exaggerated expectations. A lame-duck President Donald Trump retains the key powers over trade, tech, and foreign policy.

“Trump retains extensive foreign policy powers and a legislative veto,” says Javier Carbonell, a policy analyst at the European Policy Center. “His reaction remains unpredictable: domestic constraints could even encourage greater international activism. Europeans should not mistake electoral change for a return to transatlantic normality.”

title: What it takes to get Europe on a bike
content: On 22 September in Turin, Italy, a car driver hit and killed a seven-year-old boy cycling to school. “That could have been me, or my daughter, or anyone, really. Because that place is dangerous,” resident Maria Cristina Caimotto told us. Every morning since then, Caimotto has joined a crowd of people on bikes in the street where the tragedy took place to show solidarity with the family, but also to ask for safer streets and fewer cars. “We cannot erase what happened. We can only do everything we can so that it does not happen again,” she said. Backed by 13 civil society associations, the activists want Turin to move away from its dependence on cars. It’s ambitious, but not impossible: a similar tragedy helped push the Netherlands to become the cycling country it is today. Until the 1970s, the Netherlands was full of cars. In 1971, a six-year-old was killed cycling to school, and her father's newspaper article launched the “Stop de Kindermoord” (Stop the Child Murder) campaign against children dying in traffic. title: On the Ground in the Final Days Before Trump’s Midterm Debacle
content:
Jacob Hawk leaned over the plastic fencing to get Vivek Ramaswamy’s attention as the Republican candidate for Ohio governor moved down the line shaking hands at the Ohio University branch campus in Chillicothe, six days before the midterm elections. Hawk held onto Ramaswamy’s hand and started trying to tell him everything he was dealing with, everything he wanted the Republican candidates gathered there to help him with.

Hawk, 39, told him that he was a self-employed landscaper who was having a hard time with the high cost of fuel. He told him that he was raising three young kids from two different moms, mostly on his own. He told him of his worries for his 9-year-old son, who was autistic and underweight and suffered from a two-year delay in brain development.

title: New Congress must prioritize press freedom
content:
Dear Friend of Press Freedom:

This week’s midterm elections showed that Americans want Congress to rein in the Trump administration’s abuses — including those against the press and First Amendment. After all, crooked officials attack the press precisely because journalism interferes with whatever other nefarious plans they may have in mind. Read on for more on how you can encourage lawmakers from both parties to prioritize press freedom, as well as about other developments from an important week in the fight against censorship.

The next Congress will surely spend plenty of time investigating the Trump administration’s unconstitutional and corrupt practices when it comes to the press — as it should. But that’s not nearly enough. It also needs to pass the systemic fixes long sought by press freedom advocates. The need for these reforms has never been clearer.

title: OPINION: A UN for All? Asia’s Inclusion Must Be a Priority for the Next Secretary-General
content:
By Shihana Mohamed*

NEW YORK | 6 November 2026 (IDN) — “Outside these walls, people are not asking whether the United Nations still exists. They are asking whether it works.”

Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh, President of the United Nations General Assembly, warned the international community in his opening remarks at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA 81).

The theme of UNGA 81 was “Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.” It was an attempt to repair a fracturing multilateral system and demonstrate the UN’s ability to deliver meaningful results for all.

However, statements by Asian leaders at the session highlighted several concerns. They questioned whether the UN can truly serve all nations effectively while significant inequalities persist in global decision-making.

At UNGA 81, Asia’s major powers called for reforms to global governance, challenging existing imbalances in representation and the distribution of global influence.

title: JSN:n kokouksesta lehdistölle kolme langettavaa
content:
Julkisen sanan neuvosto teki marraskuun kokouksessaan kolme langettavaa ja kaksi vapauttavaa päätöstä.

Tekniikan Maailma julkaisi autoilijoiden ja pyöräilijöiden välisiä väistämissääntöjä koskevan väitteen, jonka neuvosto arvioi olennaiseksi asiavirheeksi. Lehti ei korjannut virhettä lukijansa pyynnöstä huolimatta. Alueviesti-lehden saama langettava päätös puolestaan johtui mielipidekirjoitukseen sisältyneistä, susia koskeneista asiavirheistä, joita ei korjattu Journalistin ohjeiden edellyttämällä tavalla. Neuvosto katsoi Alueviestin myös laiminlyöneen rooliaan huolehtia osaltaan siitä, että yhteiskunnallista keskustelua käydään tosiasioiden pohjalta.

Kolmas marraskuun kokouksessa tehty langettava päätös koski SeutuMajakka-lehteä, joka oli julkaissut samalla sivulla paikallisen yrityksen mainoksen ja yrityksestä kertoneen jutun. Vaikka kyse oli lehden mukaan vahingosta, neuvosto arvioi piilomainonnan kynnyksen ylittyneen.

title: Mikä saa minut aina puolustamaan maatani?
content:
Otsikon kysymyksen minulle esitti eräs nuori länsiuusmaalainen kutsuntojen yhteydessä tänä vuonna. Kysymys on monella tapaa pysäyttävä, ja on ikävää, että maailmanpoliittinen tilanne on sellainen, että nuoremme joutuvat pohtimaan tällaisia asioita.

Minulle vastaus on hyvin selkeä. Suomi on kotimaani, ja arvostan kaikkea sitä, mitä olen tältä maalta saanut. Arvostan luontoamme, demokratiaamme ja vapauttamme. Mutta ennen kaikkea arvostan suomalaisia ja meidän kulttuuriamme.

Niin, kulttuuriamme.

Kulttuuri on meille suomalaisille yhteinen asia, joka yhdistää meitä. Ajan saatossa kulttuurimme on muovautunut, mutta kaikki suomalaiset tuntevat Pekat ja Pätkät sekä komisario Palmun elokuvat. Ne ovat osa yhteistä kulttuuriperintöämme ja luoneet perustaa sille, mistä me suomalaiset pidämme ja mistä tunnistamme itsemme.

Itse kannan tällä hetkellä suurta huolta siitä, ettei kulttuurin merkitystä ymmärretä riittävästi huoltovarmuuden näkökulmasta. Kulttuurin ja taiteen voima on paljon suurempi kuin usein ajattelemme.

title: Tekijänoikeusbarometri 2026: Tekijänoikeudet ja luova työ ovat yhä arvossaan
content:
Lähes kolme neljästä kyselyyn vastanneista suomalaisesta katsoo, että tekoälyn kouluttamiseen käytetyistä ihmisten luomista teoksista tulee maksaa korvaus niiden tekijöille ja esittäjille. Näin kertoo lokakuussa julkaistu Tekijänoikeusbarometri 2026, joka selvittää muun muassa kansalaisten asenteita tekijänoikeuksia ja piratismia kohtaan.

Taloustutkimuksen toteuttaman Tekijänoikeusbarometrin vastaajista suurin osa (90 %) katsoo, että luovan työn tekijöille tulee maksaa korvaus sen mukaan, kuinka paljon heidän teoksiaan hyödynnetään. Tekoälyn osalta lähes 74 prosenttia on sitä mieltä, että tekijöille tulee maksaa tekoälyn kouluttamiseen käytetyistä teoksista. Eri mieltä asiasta on vain vajaa kahdeksan prosenttia.

Valtaosa kyselyyn vastanneista kansalaisista (81 %) katsoo myös, että tunnetun taiteilijan tai esittäjän persoonallista tyyliä ei saa hyödyntää tekoälysisällöissä ilman lupaa. Vuonna 2025 näin ajatteli 75 prosenttia vastaajista.

title: YK:n vuotuinen ilmastokokous alkaa uudessa tilanteessa – 1,5 asteen tavoite on karkaamassa, ja nyt pitäisi tehdä jo muutakin kuin neuvotella
content:
Yleisö nousi seisomaan ja hurrasi, kun Ranskan ulkoministeri Laurent Fabius löi puheenjohtajan nuijansa pöytään joulukuussa 2015. Pariisin ilmastosopimus oli hyväksytty.  

Pitkän väännön jälkeen sopimukseen oli saatu kirjattua lauseke, jonka mukaan maailman maat sitoutuisivat pitämään maapallon keskilämpötilan nousun alle kahdessa asteessa esiteolliseen aikaan verrattuna ja pyrkisivät rajoittamaan nousun alle 1,5 asteeseen. 

11 vuotta myöhemmin hurraahuudot ovat vähissä. Turkin Antalyassa alkaa maanantaina YK:n 31. ilmastokokous eli COP31, jossa joudutaan ensimmäistä kertaa myöntämään, että yhdessä keskeisessä Pariisin ilmastosopimuksen tavoitteessa on ainakin toistaiseksi epäonnistuttu: YK:n ympäristöohjelma UNEP kertoi tänä syksynä, että 1,5 asteen ylittäminen on nyt ”väistämätöntä”. 

Mitä se oikeastaan tarkoittaa? 

1,5 asteen ylittyminen ei ole yllätys tutkijoille eikä kenellekään ilmastouutisia seuraavallekaan. Siitä on varoiteltu jo pitkään. Nyt asia on kuitenkin ensimmäistä kertaa käytännössä varma, ja se tuo uuden ulottuvuuden ilmastopolitiikkaan.

title: JYET Strategialähtöinen osaamisen kehittäminen museoalalla 2027
content:
Museoiden tehtävä on vaalia menneisyyttä, mutta niiden oma tulevaisuus edellyttää jatkuvaa uudistumista. Digitalisaatio, tekoäly, muuttuvat yleisösuhteet ja kasvavat odotukset haastavat museoita kehittämään toimintaansa. Samalla on huolehdittava siitä, että arvokas asiantuntijuus säilyy ja siirtyy eteenpäin.

JYET Strateginen osaamisen johtaminen museoalalla -koulutuksessa kehität valmiuksiasi ennakoida osaamistarpeita, tunnistaa organisaatiosi keskeiset kyvykkyydet ja johtaa uudistumista suunnitelmallisesti. Opit yhdistämään strategiset tavoitteet henkilöstön osaamisen kehittämiseen sekä rakentamaan toimintatapoja, joissa oppiminen tapahtuu osana jokapäiväistä työtä.

Neljän lähikoulutuspäivän ja omaan työhön sovellettavien tehtävien aikana rakennat omalle museo-organisaatiollesi strategisen osaamisen kehittämisen ja uudistumisen suunnitelman. Saat konkreettisia välineitä osaamisen johtamiseen, henkilöstön osallistamiseen ja kehittämistoimenpiteiden toteuttamiseen.

title: Don’t wash your laundry at teatime – why planning energy use can reduce your bills
content:
For decades, judging a home’s energy performance meant asking one question: how much does it use? Labels such as energy performance certificates still ask only that.

But homes are changing. Add solar panels, a battery or an electric car, and a house starts to generate, store and sell electricity. Meanwhile, what that electricity costs depends more and more on the clock. Since June 2026, Ireland’s largest suppliers have had to offer tariffs that change every half hour. In the UK, households pay about 26p for each unit they buy, but solar owners can be paid as little as a few pence for each unit they sell.

The question has shifted from how much energy is being used to when is it being consumed? Every building is now an energy system. The clearest example of what that means is a long way from Europe.

In Pakistan, an estimated 7.3 million households, nearly one in five, now have solar panels. In the year to June 2025, panels on homes, shops, farm sheds and small factories produced the equivalent of 46% of all electricity sold through the national grid. Three lessons stand out.

title: 10 years after Leonard Cohen’s passing, his grappling with the divine lives on
content:
Right now, Leonard Cohen is on many of his fans’ minds.

The Canadian poet, novelist and singer-songwriter died Nov. 7, 2016, just one day before United States President Donald Trump was first elected.

Ten years later, as the Democrat “blue wave” hopes to close the bracket on a president who once memed himself as Jesus personified, Cohen’s legacy has become effortlessly epic — even biblical — in quite a different way.

Tribute gatherings for the singer abound. Cohen was the subject of a sold-out event at the Toronto International Festival of Authors at the end of October.

Adam Cohen’s family tour, which began in Canada this month and reaches Europe in winter 2027, pairs his father’s music with archival photos and film.

Ottawa’s Gladstone Theatre advertised their “Ten Years Gone” commemoration with a question quite suggestive to people like me who study the evolution of sacred texts: “What would Cohen say today?”

title: Syytteet laittoman IPTV-palvelun ylläpidosta ja katselutunnusten myynnistä
content:
Syyttäjä nosti keskiviikkona 4.10.2026 syytteet kahdesta epäillystä tekijänoikeusrikoksesta. Syytettyinä olevat kaksi henkilöä olivat ensimmäisen syytteen mukaan hankkineet laittomasta palvelusta sisältöjen katselu- ja kuuntelutunnuksia sekä myyneet niitä ilman oikeudenhaltijoiden lupaa omille asiakkailleen. Myös omaan käyttöön hankittujen sisältöpakettien katseluoikeuksia myytiin tekijöiden perustaman palvelun asiakkaille.

Toisen syytteen mukaan samat henkilöt olivat perustaneet ja ylläpitäneet laitonta IPTV-palvelua niin, että palvelun asiakkaille olisi maksua vastaan tarjottu lukuisia elokuvia ja televisiokanavia sisältöineen ilman oikeudenhaltijoiden lupaa. Epäillään, että rikokset on tehty ansiotarkoituksessa.

Kyse on ensimmäisestä Suomessa rikosprosessin kohteeksi joutuneesta laittomasta IPTV-palvelusta. Ruotsissa on ehditty antaa rikostuomio jo yli kymmenen laittoman palvelun ylläpidolle. TTVK edustaa rikosasiassa asianomistajina olevia lähettäjäyrityksiä sekä kotimaisia tuotantoyhtiöitä.

title: YK:n pääsihteerin raportti: Aseellisissa konflikteissa kuolleiden naisten ja tyttöjen määrä kaksinkertaistunut vuodesta 2021
content:
Viime vuonna konflikteissa kuoli yli 37 000 siviiliä. Joka neljäs heistä oli nainen tai tyttö. Naisten ja tyttöjen osuus kuolleista on kaksinkertaistunut vuoteen 2021 verrattuna, ilmenee 26.10.2026 julkaistusta YK:n pääsihteerin vuoden 2026 Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuus -raportista.

Tällä hetkellä noin 750 miljoonaa naista ja tyttöä elää alle 50 kilometrin päässä aktiivisesta konfliktialueesta. Määrä on kasvanut 40 miljoonalla vuodesta 2024 ja on suurempi kuin kertaakaan vuoden 1990 jälkeen.

”Yhä useammat naiset ja tytöt elävät sotien keskellä – enemmän kuin kertaakaan vuosikymmeniin. Samaan aikaan sotilasmenot kasvavat ja kehitysyhteistyöhön suunnattu rahoitus vähenee, vaikka naisten johtajuuteen, konfliktien ehkäisyyn ja rauhanrakentamiseen investoiminen on tärkeämpää kuin koskaan”, sanoo UN Womenin pääjohtaja Sima Bahous.

Sodan keskellä eläville naisille ja tytöille uhka ei rajoitu pommeihin ja aseellisiin iskuihin. YK:n vahvistamien konflikteihin liittyvien seksuaalisen väkivallan tapausten määrä lähes nelinkertaistui vuosina 2022–2025. Sodat myös syventävät naisten köyhyyttä ja lisäävät heidän tekemänsä palkattoman hoiva- ja kotityön määrää.

title: Paraguay: Institutional crisis demands a human rights-centred response
content:
In response to the financial and political crisis triggered by the initiation of resolution proceedings against a financial institution by the Central Bank of Paraguay (BCP), which has sparked public protests and led to impeachment proceedings against President Santiago Peña, Amnesty International calls on the Paraguayan authorities to ensure the protection of those affected, guarantee transparency and respect the right to peaceful protest.

“Behind this crisis are people who cannot access their savings, families facing uncertainty, and workers and pensioners whose rights may be at risk. The State’s response must put people at the centre, provide effective solutions and ensure that no economic or political interest takes precedence over their rights,” said Ana Piquer, Amnesty International’s Director for the Americas.

title: ‘Simply staggering’: Rapidly developing ‘super El Niño’ on track to peak in December
content:
The ongoing “super El Niño” is likely to peak at the end of 2026 and push average global temperatures to record levels next year.

That is according to Carbon Brief’s latest “state of the climate” update, which analyses El Niño forecasts from more than a dozen climate models, as well as six global temperature datasets.

Dr Zeke Hausfather, Carbon Brief’s climate science contributor, described this year’s El Niño as “simply staggering” when answering questions from CB+ members during a CB Connect “ask me anything” session.

El Niño is a naturally occurring climate pattern in the tropical Pacific that releases heat from the ocean into the atmosphere and temporarily boosts global temperatures. 

This year’s El Niño event – which has been underway since June – has already broken a number of records and reshaped the world’s weather, fuelling fires in Indonesia and “super typhoons” in the west Pacific.

The strength of an El Niño is tracked using the “Niño3.4 anomaly”, which is a measure of how much warmer sea surface temperatures are than average in a section of the central Pacific.
snippet: The ongoing “super El Niño” is likely to peak at the end of 2026 and push average global temperatures to record levels next year.

title: Google Forcing AI on Students Is BS
content:
Google is rightfully facing blowback for forcing K-12 schools to enable AI if they wanted to keep using Google search. The company quickly backtracked and decoupled and turned off the services by default, but made it clear search will continue to be just another AI chatbot. This mandate forces an ultimatum on educators: accept generative AI or de-google your school.

Students, teachers, and parents across the U.S. are now years into an argument about how schools should respond to the growth of AI-enabled tools. Google decided to skip this debate and take this choice from schools. In August it activated AI chatbot Gemini for 150 million K-12 students on Google Classroom, leaving educators scrambling to respond. A few months later, Google introduced a new way to turn it off — but now administrators would also be turning off Google search.

Google walked this back somewhat, clarifying that Gemini, Gemini notebook, and Search will have their own controls and will be off by default. But because of Google’s broader approach to force AI on all search users, this change is still an example of a tech monopolist pushing unwanted changes into the classroom.

title: Suden DNA-näytekeräys alkaa joulukuussa, koulutusta tarjolla vapaaehtoisille
content:
Suden DNA-näytteitä kerätään jälleen talvella 2026–2027. Tällä keräyskaudella näytteiden kerääminen alkaa 1.12. ja jatkuu helmikuun loppuun. Kiintiömetsästysalueilla keräys alkaa 1.1.2027.

Kaikille suden DNA-näytekeräyksestä kiinnostuneille järjestetään Teams-koulutus torstaina 19.11. klo 18-19.30. Koulutukseen voi osallistua kuka tahansa aiheesta kiinnostunut, eikä osallistuminen sido ryhtymään näytekerääjäksi.

Kaikkia vapaaehtoisia DNA-näytekerääjiä kannustetaan rekisteröitymään kerääjiksi tällä kaudella. Rekisteröityneet saavat keräysohjeet ja tietoa keräyksen etenemisestä suoraan omaan sähköpostiinsa sekä oman kerääjätunnuksen. Jokaiselle keräyskaudelle rekisteröidytään erikseen, ja kaudesta 2027–2028 alkaen kaikkien kerääjien tulee rekisteröityä.

Keräyksessä painotetaan erityisesti tammi–helmikuussa kerättyjä näytteitä, sillä ne antavat mahdollisimman ajantasaisen kuvan susikannasta maaliskuun tilannetta kuvaavaa kanta-arviota varten. Kiintiömetsästysalueilla pyynnin jälkeen kerätyt näytteet auttavat selvittämään, millainen susikanta alueelle on jäänyt.

title: Asiakkaalle maksu heti: Kultakiertue siirtyy pikamaksuihin
content:
Pikamaksussa raha siirtyy pankista toiseen sekunneissa, eikä sen kulku ole sidottu pankkipäiviin tai pankkien aukioloaikoihin. Tavallinen tilisiirto voi näkyä vastaanottajalla vasta seuraavana pankkipäivänä, mikä on tarkoittanut asiakkaalle odottamista erityisesti iltaisin ja viikonloppuisin tehdyissä kaupoissa.

Uudistuksen jälkeen kauppasumma lähetetään asiakkaan ilmoittamalle tilille samalla hetkellä, kun kauppa on vahvistettu. Asiakas voi seurata maksun saapumista omasta verkkopankistaan tai pankkisovelluksestaan.

Se, kuinka nopeasti maksu näkyy tilillä, riippuu lopulta vastaanottavan pankin järjestelmistä. Useimmissa tapauksissa summa näkyy tilillä muutamassa minuutissa. Pikamaksu on asiakkaalle veloitukseton, eikä se vaadi asiakkaalta toimenpiteitä tavallisen tilinumeron ilmoittamisen lisäksi.

– Kullan myyminen on monelle iso päätös, ja kun kauppa on tehty, asiakkaan pitää voida luottaa siihen, että rahat ovat jo matkalla. Pikamaksun ansiosta kenenkään ei tarvitse enää odottaa seuraavaan pankkipäivään, vaan maksu lähtee tilille heti, sanoo Sanna Mämmi Kultakiertueen Head of PR & Communications.

title: British-Turkish novelist Elif Shafak receives Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Awareness of Cultural Heritage 2026 in Lisbon
content:
“Literature has a very gentle but very profound power and resilience. It gives us hope and continues to connect us beyond all borders of identity, geography and time,” stated Elif Shafak, renowned British-Turkish novelist and storyteller after receiving the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Public Awareness of Cultural Heritage 2026 at a ceremony held on 5 November at the Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon, Portugal.

High-level representatives of the partners and supporters of the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award – namely the President of Centro Nacional de Cultura, Maria Calado, the Secretary General of Europa Nostra, Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović, and the representative of the Gulbenkian Foundation in the Award Jury, Guilherme d’Oliveira Martins – as well as the Mayor of Lisbon, Carlos Moedas, addressed the audience. The ceremony was attended by some 200 people. Among the guests of honour was the former President of Portugal, Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa.

title: Metallia ja dreampopia yhdistelevä Sisar haluaa olla raskas mutta ei aggressiivinen
content:
Suomessa tehdään väkilukuun suhteutettuna eniten metallimusiikkia maailmassa. Silti vain harva yhtye on keksinyt kokeilla, mitä metallin ja dreampopin yhdistämisestä seuraa.

Helsinkiläisduo Sisar keksi. Sen tuoreella debyyttilevyllä Valo valtaa vielä kaiken raskaat kitarat ja teolliset konerummut kietoutuvat keveisiin, kerroksellisiin ja toismaailmallisiin poplaulumelodioihin. Soundissa voi kuulla kaikuja esimerkiksi Karinan tai Saran äänimaisemista, mutta silti levy kuulostaa vain ja ainoastaan tekijöiltään.

”Puhuttiin alusta asti, että tehtäisiin raskasta musiikkia, joka ei olisi välttämättä aggressiivista. Raskaus yhdistyy hyvin myös tunteellisempaan matskuun”, Sisaren kitaristi ja rumpuohjelmoija Remi Rousselle perustelee yhtyeensä tyylivalintaa.

Laulaja-basisti Nora Moberg korostaa, että oli jo pitkään halunnut laulaa raskaammassa yhtyeessä, mutta omalla tyylillään.

”Ääneni tai vahvuuteni laulajana ei ole hevi-ilmaisussa, joten ehkä tämä juttu rakentui pitkälti myös sen ympärille, mitä ääneni mahdollistaa. Olen aina tykännyt leikitellä äänelläni ja laulaa tahallani ei-niin-odotettavasti”, hän kertoo.

title: Rights on the Ballot Alongside US Congressional Elections
content:
Alongside the high-profile congressional and gubernatorial races decided during the United States midterm elections on November 3, human rights were at issue in several state and local ballot measures across the country. 

In Virginia, voters adopted a measure to automatically restore voting rights to people with felony convictions upon release from prison, ending a lifetime ban that had been in place since the Jim Crow era.

Arizona voters rejected and Wisconsin voters approved measures to end diversity, equity, and inclusion practices in education, employment, contracts, and administration, mirroring Trump administration initiatives to dismantle programs to address ongoing impacts of historical discrimination based on race and ethnicity. Vermont voters approved an amendment providing equal protection to individuals regardless of their race, ethnicity, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or national origin.

Meanwhile, Missouri voters rejected an effort to restrict the right to abortion care and measures to safeguard abortion rights were successful in Nevada and Virginia but failed in Idaho.

title: K-podd 97: Offergåvorna från Unna Sájvva
content:
Den samiska offerplatsen Unna Sájjva ligger belägen vid en sjö i södraste delarna av Gällivare kommun. År 1915 bestämde sig arkeologen Gustaf Hallström för att gräva ut platsen. Han förde sedan hundratals föremål till Statens historiska museum i Stockholm, där de legat arkiverade fram till nu.
Det här avsnittet av K-podd handlar om hur offergåvorna från Unna Sájjva ska få komma hem igen.

Riksantikvarieämbetet har haft i uppdrag av regeringen att informera om möjligheten att söka bidrag för återlämnandeprocesser, och erbjuda vägledning till organisationer som företräder de nationella minoriteterna, inklusive urfolket samerna.

Ett 40-tal samer från området kring Unna Sájjva med eldsjälen Kerstin Andersson i spetsen, har tilldelats det hittills största bidraget för återlämnande. Tillsammans med Statens historiska museer och Ájjte fjäll- och samemuseum i Jokkmokk ser Kerstin Andersson nu till att offergåvorna får komma hem igen.

title: France’s Open Science Strategy: National Ambition, Local Delivery, and AI
content:
Blog post by Camille Françoise and Ophélie Wang

Published in September 2026 and presented by the Ministry of Research, the new French Strategy for Open Science (2026-2033) follows two previous “national plans” for Open Science (OS), dating back to 2018 and 2021. The Strategy spans 100 pages and cites more than 100 publications. It is a reflective text setting out France’s ambitions for OS, offering both a review of nearly ten years of public policy support in this area and an overview of the main priorities for the years ahead.

This article focuses on one key conclusion and one forward-looking perspective from the Strategy, highlighting their potential relevance for other countries in the European context and, more specifically, for the work carried out under the Knowledge Rights 21 (KR21) programme.

The Strategy sets out the challenges that OS still faces and recognises that the barriers remain both strong and diverse: publishing practices and cultures across disciplines, reluctance to share data, lack of funding, and others. These barriers were identified through a survey asking universities and research institutions to name the factors they considered the main hurdles to OS.

title: De får Kulturfondens pris på svenska dagen
content:
På Svenska dagen prisbelönar Svenska kulturfonden eldsjälar som gjort insatser för kultur eller utbildning på svenska i sin region. I år får Dan Idman det nyländska svenskadagenpriset, Nicklas Lantz det åboländska priset och Olena Galchenko det österbottniska.

Svenska kulturfondens svenskadagenpris är på 6 000 euro vardera. I varje region utses en pristagare.

Nylands svenska kulturfonds svenskadagenpris på 6 000 euro

Scenartisten Dan Idman har i över fyra decennier varit en eldsjäl inom nyländsk amatörteater. Strålkastarljuset föll på honom redan då han var skolelev och i mitten av 1980-talet var Lurens platsen för hans sommarkvällar. Sedan dess har ridån aldrig gått ner.

I Dan Idman bor komikern och skurken sida vid sida. I ett sjuttiotal teaterproduktioner har han haft otaliga minnesvärda roller – han har fått salonger att gunga av skratt och i nästa sekund att rysa. 

Men Dan Idman har också regisserat, dramatiserat och översatt pjäser. Han har penslat fram ansikten i sminkspegeln, klätt ensembler och viktigast av allt – han har inspirerat flera generationer av barn och unga att ta plats på teaterscener i Nyland.

title: Democrats Should Not Revert To The Status Quo Ante
content:
The great blue wave that washed over America in the election should not lure Democrats into the delusion that they are once again lovingly embraced by the body politic.

Rather, it should be seen for what it is: a widespread counter-revolt at the ballot box against all that Trumpism has wrought — a heightened crisis of affordability exacerbated by trade wars and a war of choice with Iran, self-dealing corruption, politicization of the rule of law and an unbounded, mean-spirited mega-megalomania rarely seen in mature democracies.

The worst mistake Democrats can make is to misread their mandate. That mandate is to narrow the margin of maneuver of a wounded lame-duck presidency, derail the trajectory toward autocracy and clean up the mess. It is not to return to the status quo ante of cultural elitism, censorious identity politics, lax borders and hyper-globalization that opened the path to Trumpism in the first place.
snippet: The great blue wave that washed over America in the election should not lure Democrats into the delusion that they are once again lovingly embraced by the body politic.

title: Was Homer’s Ithaca Really an Island?: New Research Challenges a 2,000-Year-Old Assumption
content:
Even if we didn’t make it to a screening of Christopher Nolan’s big-screen adaptation this past summer — and indeed, even if we’ve never read Homer’s original epic at all — we know that the Odyssey tells the story of a ten-year-long journey back to Ithaca. The narrative’s urgency doesn’t arise from the fact that its protagonist, the king Odysseus, has classes at Cornell to teach. In fact, he may not even be trying to get back to the extant Greek island celebrated for bearing that same name. So, at least, argues a recent paper by two distinguished professors, Cambridge’s James Diggle and the University of Aberdeen’s John Underhill. You can read “Was Homer’s Ithaca an Island?” at the online journal Antigone.

Alternatively, you can watch the new video from classicist-novelist Honor Cargill-Martin above. The real Greek island of Ithaca, or Ithaki, with its picturesque hamlets and limestone monoliths, “actually doesn’t match, pretty much at all, the description that Homer gives us of Ithaca,” she says.

title: Mélenchon squares up to Brussels in election manifesto
content:
PARIS — French leftist presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon wants a radical overhaul of EU rules that would set him on a collision course with Brussels.

The far-left leader, who has enjoyed a recent surge in the polls ahead of the 2027 election, pitched a series of measures to fundamentally rethink the EU’s agenda in his presidential platform unveiled Friday. Mélenchon also said he would disobey current EU rules that would prevent him from implementing his platform if elected.

Proposing a “new deal” for Europe, Mélenchon wants to redraft the treaties, ditch core parts of the EU’s rulebook — including debt and deficit limits — suspend competition rules for public services such as energy, transport and telecoms, and loosen state aid laws.

“We will immediately implement our program at the national level. This will therefore require a confrontation with European institutions,” according to the manifesto from Mélenchon’s France Unbowed. “This also means disobeying rules blocking [us] whenever necessary.”

title: “Metsän voisi hakata datakeskuksen alta” – Elo ja Pitko tyrmäävät ennallistamissuunnitelman
content:
Vihreiden kansanedustajat Tiina Elo ja Jenni Pitko arvostelevat jyrkästi ennallistamissuunnitelmaa, jonka luonnoksen hallitus eilen hyväksyi. Heidän mukaansa keskeinen ongelma on se, että hallitus päätti rajata heikentämättömyysvelvoitteen koskemaan vain Natura-alueita, jotka jo ovat tiukan suojelun piirissä.

"Luonnontilaa saisi siis edelleen heikentää suojelualueiden ulkopuolella ilman ennallistamis- tai kompensaatiovelvoitteita. Metsän voisi esimerkiksi hakata datakeskuksen alta tai jatkaa vesistöjä rehevöittäviä ojituksia", Elo sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

Luontojärjestöt pitävät Suomen suunnitelmaluonnosta EU:n ennallistamisasetuksen vastaisena. Pitkon mukaan esitys on rakennettu ennallistamisen kannalta väärille perusteille.

"Hallitus on kaikkien perusperiaatteiden vastaisesti päättänyt tehdä heikentämättömyydestä vapaaehtoista. Eli luonnon kadottaminen ja pilaaminen on edelleen sallittua ja laillista samalla kun pienillä resursseilla yritetään epätoivoisesti paikata tilannetta", Pitko sanoo tiedotteessa.

Tiina Elo muistuttaa metsäluonnon köyhtymisestä. Valtion vanhojen metsien suojelukaan ei etene, vaikka pääministeri Orpo ennen vaaleja niin lupasi.

title: In Conversation with Jean Lambert, England and Wales
content:
Jean Lambert is a long-standing member of the Green Party of England and Wales, where she has held a number of posts of responsibility. She served as London’s Green Party MEP for four terms (1999-2019) and was a member of the Employment and Social Affairs Committee and the Civil Liberties Committee. Jean chaired the EP’s Delegation to the Countries of South Asia for ten years and took part in a number of Election Observation missions. Prior to her election to the EP, Jean worked as a secondary school teacher in East London. Jean is now a Trustee of the European Network on Statelessness (ENS) and a Board member of a Brussels-based organisation promoting citizens’ rights. She also recently served on the Committee of the European Green Party. She is an avid reader of crime fiction and loves dancing. 

In this interview, Jean Lambert reflects on five decades of Green politics, from its early roots to its influence on the European agenda. She explores the lessons of European cooperation, the challenges of delivering a socially just green transition, and why the movement must keep climate at its core while rediscovering its original imagination and ambition.

title: Kuvakaappauksesta taulukoksi, ehdoista ohjeeksi – tekoäly kiertotalouden arjessa
content:
CIRCULAI on valtakunnallinen ESR+-rahoitteinen hanke, joka tuo tekoälyn mahdollisuudet osaksi suomalaisten kiertotalousyritysten arkea. Tavoitteena on vahvistaa alan työntekijöiden tekoälylukutaitoa ja rohkaista hyödyntämään tekoälyä työn, prosessien ja liiketoiminnan kehittämisessä – käytännönläheisesti ja turvallisesti.

Vaikeasti luettava järjestelmänäkymä, aikaa vievä Excel-tehtävä ja ohje, joka pitäisi saada kirjoitettua. CIRCULAI-hankkeen haastatteluissa generatiivisen tekoälyn käytännön hyödyt löytyvät usein juuri tällaisista arkisista tilanteista. Kiertotalouden parissa työskentelevät ovat ottaneet tekoälyä avuksi tiedon jäsentämiseen, kirjoittamiseen ja teknisten pulmien ratkaisemiseen.

Esimerkit kertovat myös siitä, missä apua vielä tarvitaan. Tekoälyn tekemä virhe pitää huomata, ja nopeasti syntynyt teksti voi vaatia niin paljon muokkaamista, että hyöty jää pieneksi. Käyttökohteen valinta ratkaisee paljon.

Eräässä yrityksessä toiminnan aikataulutiedot olivat järjestelmässä muodossa, jonka lukeminen vaati eri tietojen yhdistelyä. Työntekijä otti näkymästä kuvakaappauksen ja pyysi ChatGPT:tä tekemään siitä selkeämmän taulukon.

title: Europe’s Sanctions on Russia: Riddled With Loopholes
content:
Over half of the names the EU added to its sanctions in October are aimed at the production chain of the ballistic missiles now targeting Ukrainian cities, chief diplomat Kaja Kallas said. The list of 826 Russian companies and 743 of their chief executives is the EU’s largest-ever set of military-industrial listings. 

A couple of days later, the Council added 12 more names for helping Russia evade sanctions, among them oil intermediaries in the United Arab Emirates and India. 

Yet October avoided the politically difficult decisions. No new sector-wide trade ban, and nothing on oil or gas.  

Europe has two problems with its Russia sanctions: any one of the bloc’s 27 members can insist that its special interests are protected, and the rules already agreed are enforced unevenly. 

July showed how the first problem works. The package passed only after Greece secured an exemption allowing EU operators to carry Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) to third countries under pre-invasion contracts. A proposed ban on Russian fish imports was dropped along the way. 

Every sector-wide measure affects businesses among the 27 members. Every capital has a veto.

title: Justice, Diversity & Inclusion: Start Here
content:
Welcome to the Justice, Diversity and Inclusion topic in the Commons Social Change Library. We believe that strong movements are made up of diverse participants, each bringing their particular talents, perspectives, and community connections. Developing such movements requires an appreciation for the value of diversity, as well as experience including, and working in solidarity with, those who are marginalised by the dominant assumed common culture. The restructuring of power relations and real engagement with justice concerns are necessary for true inclusion.

To help navigate within the broad scope this topic includes, we’ve outlined examples from four types of resources:

  • resources that clarify key concepts used in movements seeking to improve diversity and inclusion practices;
  • resources to help those building capacity to recognise and resist oppression of all forms, such as by seeking out diverse perspectives and recognising and leveraging privileges.
  • advice for taking action, including specific acts of inclusion, acts of solidarity, and acts of resistance.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has revived the midnight game launch – but was it worth the wait?
content:
When our writer found himself among the hundreds on Oxford Street hoping to get their hands on early copies and collectibles, it was a heartwarming reminder of the shared experience of fandom

• The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review – a dream come true

It is Thursday night and I am sat blurry-eyed and runny nosed outside the Argos on Oxford Street. Incredibly, I am far from alone. This is not some strange protest against the popular retailer. When the clock strikes midnight, the lavish 4K Switch 2 remake of beloved N64 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released, and I have joined a lengthy queue of about 500 fans desperate to snag early copies. There are similar events taking place across the world, from Melbourne to Mexico City; at key locations, Nintendo has senior executives waiting at the tills.

title: Trump Official Who Wants Data Centers on Public Lands Has Tens of Millions Invested in AI Industry
content:
The Trump administration has likened the need to build out the nation’s artificial intelligence infrastructure to the Manhattan Project, the World War II effort that produced the world’s first atomic bomb.

The White House’s point person on the effort, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, has spoken of the “AI arms race” with China as an existential issue for the nation. “AI is manufacturing intelligence, and, if we don’t manufacture more intelligence than our adversaries, it affects every job, every company and every industry,” he said during his Senate confirmation hearing in January 2025.

But advancing the administration’s AI objectives also could benefit Burgum’s own finances.

Much of his wealth is held in Arthur Ventures, an investment firm he co-founded, according to his 2026 financial disclosure form, which has not been previously reported. Between $18.1 million and $64.4 million of those investments are in AI companies, according to an analysis of the companies’ marketing materials shared with ProPublica by public lands advocacy group Save Our Parks. (Government financial disclosure forms allow filers to report wide ranges instead of the specific value of their investments.)

title: Global Voices condemns the attacks on Albanian fact-checking service Faktoje
content:
Faktoje is a respected member of the international fact-checking community

Originally published on Global Voices

Since October 27, at least 20 online media outlets and social media accounts in Albania have been waging a coordinated attack against the staff of fact-checking media service Faktoje Center, based in Tirana. A partner of Global Voices, Faktoje has been promoting accountability based on the right to information and transparency since 2018.

Faktoje and its team members, in particular its director, Klodiana Kapo, are facing a series of coordinated attacks from media outlets that have been circulating and reproducing articles that question Faktoje’s funding, financial management and independence, using its publicly available financial statements to cast doubt on the organisation’s credibility.

title: ESSAY: While the World Burns …
content:
By Franz Baumann*

This essay was originally published online on 2 November 2026 in Environment: Science and Policy for Sustainable Development, Taylor & Francis, under the title “While the World Burns …” DOI: 10.1080/00139157.2026.2725625.

VIENNA | 6 November 2026 (IDN) — “Our house is on fire while we avert our eyes. Nature, mutilated and plundered, can no longer regenerate and we refuse to admit it.”—President Jacques Chirac at the 2002 Earth Summit in Johannesburg, South Africa

Barry Commoner, the founder of Taylor & Francis Online, defined the Four Laws of Ecology in 1971:

Everything is connected to everything else. There is one ecosphere for all living organisms and what affects one, affects all.

Everything must go somewhere. There is no “waste” in nature and there is no “away” to which things can be thrown.

Nature knows best. Humankind has fashioned technology to improve upon nature, but such change in a natural system is likely to be detrimental to that system.

There is no such thing as a free lunch. Exploitation of nature will inevitably involve the conversion of resources from useful to useless forms.

title: AI could transform mathematics, but humans will still need to be in the loop
content:
OpenAI recently announced that one of its AI models solved one of the hardest problems in modern mathematics: the Navier–Stokes problem. The equations at the heart of this problem describe the movement of fluids like water and, according to the scientific definition, air.

The Navier-Stokes equations are essential to understanding phenomena such as ocean currents, blood circulation, and airflow over airplane wings. Yet, mathematicians have struggled for decades to determine whether coherent solutions to these equations exist.

It was for this reason that the US-based Clay Mathematics Institute, which is dedicated to disseminating mathematical knowledge, chose the Navier-Stokes problem as one of its seven Millennium Prize Problems.

These are the most important and challenging unsolved problems in modern mathematics, with a prize of US$1 million (£746,000; €895,000) offered for the first correct solution to each. A problem that resisted generations of mathematicians thus has apparently been solved by artificial intelligence.

title: We need to talk about Meta: Political interference and interests in the Brazilian elections
content: On the eve of Donald Trump’s return to the presidency of the United States, in January 2025, Meta’s founder and CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, announced that changes would be made to his company’s moderation policies in the name of “freedom of expression”, which, he said, was under threat by global pressures for what he saw as censorship. The announcement signaled a rapprochement between Meta and the far right around a common goal: the deregulation of Big Tech. Since then, growing entanglement between major technology companies and the U.S. President Donald Trump administration has shown how the private interests of a small group can override the public interest.

title: Ulkoministeri Valtonen Varsovaan
content:
Ulkoministeri Valtonen osallistuu 6. marraskuuta Itämeren valtioiden neuvoston (Council of the Baltic Sea States, CBSS) ja Ukrainan epäviralliseen ministeritapaamiseen Varsovassa, Puolassa.

Itämeren valtioiden neuvosto on vuonna 1992 perustettu Itämeren alueen maiden hallitusten välinen yhteistyöjärjestö. title: YK:n pääsihteerin Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuus-raportti: Sodat tappavat yhä enemmän naisia ja tyttöjä – mutta naiset suljetaan edelleen rauhanneuvottelujen ulkopuolelle
content:
YK:n pääsihteerin vuoden 2026 Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuus -raportti piirtää synkän kuvan maailman turvallisuustilanteesta ja sen vaikutuksista naisiin ja tyttöihin. Aseellisten konfliktien määrä on noussut korkeimmalle tasolle sitten vuoden 1945, ja yhä useampi nainen ja tyttö joutuu elämään sodan ja väkivallan keskellä.

Vuonna 2025 peräti 756 miljoonaa naista ja tyttöä eli alle 50 kilometrin päässä aktiivisesta konfliktialueesta. Määrä vastaa 19 prosenttia maailman naisista ja tytöistä ja on korkein sitten 1990-luvun.

YK dokumentoi vuoden aikana yli 37 000 siviilin kuoleman 20 aseellisessa konfliktissa. Joka neljäs kuolleista oli nainen tai tyttö.

Samaan aikaan maailman sotilasmenot nousivat ennätykselliseen 2 900 miljardiin dollariin. Sotilasmenot ovat kasvaneet jo 11 vuotta peräkkäin ja yli kaksinkertaistuneet vuoteen 2000 verrattuna.

Konflikteihin liittyvä seksuaalinen väkivalta on lisääntynyt voimakkaasti. Vuonna 2025 YK dokumentoi 9 788 tapausta, mikä on yli kaksinkertainen määrä edellisvuoteen verrattuna ja lähes nelinkertainen vuoteen 2022 verrattuna.

Todellinen määrä on todennäköisesti huomattavasti suurempi, sillä suuri osa seksuaalisesta väkivallasta jää raportoimatta.

title: UK Sex Workers Wake Up to Sites Purging Their Content Following Porn Ban
content:
Immediately after the UK banned a wide range of porn fantasies involving choking, breath-restriction, and relative roleplay, adult creators watched platforms remove hundreds of their videos — even when the creators thought they were in compliance with the law. These creators say they were blindsided by the removals, since the content didn’t seem to violate the law at all.

Creators are reporting one platform in particular, Clips4Sale, is purging content with little notice, “a precautionary measure.”   

Some creators who’ve contacted Clips4Sale to appeal these removals have shared screenshots online of the reply the platform sends: “At this time, we have implemented a general restriction on content availability in the UK to ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements,” Clips4Sale support replies, according to these screenshots, viewed by 404 Media. “This is a precautionary measure and does not necessarily indicate that your clips contain prohibited content or violate our policies. We are continuing to review affected content, and additional clips will be made available to UK buyers as they are reviewed and cleared.”

title: EU: Commission’s findings on TikTok “rabbit hole” effect must trigger fundamental changes to social media design
content:
Responding to the European Commission’s preliminary findings that TikTok is in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) because of the “rabbit hole” effect of its recommender system, Lisa Dittmer, Amnesty International Researcher on Children and Young People’s Digital Rights, said:    

“The Commission’s preliminary finding that TikTok’s ‘For You’ feed puts users’ wellbeing at risk is a welcome and urgently needed step in the fight for accountability and safer online platforms. Amnesty International’s research has repeatedly documented how TikTok draws some children into rabbit holes of depressive and suicidal ideation content. Young people and bereaved parents shared with us how TikTok’s feed normalized and exacerbated teenagers’ struggles with depression and self-harm. This should never have been allowed to happen.

title: Analysis: China’s quarterly CO2 falls 3% in largest drop since Covid
content:
China’s carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions fell by 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, as the Hormuz crisis continued to hit oil demand and coal use also dropped.

Lauri Myllyvirta, lead analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air

This was the largest quarterly reduction since the 2022 Covid lockdowns and means that China’s CO2 emissions have now fallen by an estimated 0.5% in the year to date.

The new analysis for Carbon Brief, based on official figures and commercial data, shows that coal use fell by 3% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, while oil was down 4%.

The main drivers were a fall in power-sector coal consumption, a continued sharp reduction in transport oil consumption and slowing growth in the coal-to-chemical industry.

The sharp decline in China’s CO2 emissions extends a “flat or falling” trend that began in March 2024 and has now lasted more than two years, as shown in the figure below.

The outlook for China’s CO2 emissions depends on the balance between rising energy demand, clean-energy growth and the government response to a GDP slowdown.

title: National Politics Will Never Be the Same: Juan González on How Latino Voters Remade the Political Map
content:
The midterms saw a landslide of Latinos vote for Democrats. In Texas, California, Kansas and Colorado, Latinos who had voted for Republicans just two years ago voted for Democrats in large numbers, helping secure Democratic control of both the House and the Senate. Latino lawmakers will make up about a fifth of the Democratic majority in the House. And in an historic victory, the two most populous states in the country, California and Texas, will soon be led by Democratic Latino governors.

“Texas has been suddenly transformed into a battleground state,” says Democracy Now! co-host Juan Gonzalez. “Texas has been the biggest and most important red state in the country for decades, and I’ve been predicting for years that it is the key link for achieving a realignment of national politics.”

title: Presenting 'Desire Lines: Encoding Queer Digital Futures'
content:
What does the digital future look like? Who gets to imagine it, shape it, and make it real?

Building a freer, more inclusive digital age requires not only challenging systems of surveillance and control, but also making space for creativity, community, and radical imagination. 

That's why earlier this year with the queer arts collective, we put out a call for submissions inviting people to explore the intersections of technology, identity, and digital liberation—whether that involved pointing the lens towards an underrepresented issue in digital justice efforts; sharing personal accounts of joy, pleasure, or sorrow under surveillance; or painting wide imaginations for our communities using technology for good instead of carcerality and doom.

And we’re excited to share that the project is now live! Desire Lines: Encoding Queer Digital Futures explores a digital world that dreams wilder and exists louder. Seven artists share their visions of digital liberation, spanning from early internet-coded yearning to escapist steamy chat rooms and seed-laced battle suits for revolution.
snippet: What does the digital future look like? Who gets to imagine it, shape it, and make it real?

title: Omaishoidon tukea ja kuljetuspalvelua voi hakea nyt verkossa koko Pohjois-Savossa
content:
Pohjois-Savon hyvinvointialue on laajentanut sosiaalipalvelujen digitaalista asiointia ikääntyneille suunnattuihin palveluihin. OmaSavossa voi nyt hakea sähköisesti omaishoidon tukea ja kuljetuspalvelua.

- Omaishoidon tuen ja kuljetuspalvelun hakeminen onnistuu silloin, kun asiakkaalle tai läheiselle parhaiten sopii. Digitaalisesti täytetty hakemus siirtyy suoraan ammattilaisen käsittelyyn, asiakasohjauksen palveluyksikköjohtaja Hanna Jokinen kuvaa.

Hyvinvointialueella on tällä hetkellä noin 1 650 omaishoidon tuen saajaa. Vuonna 2025 uusia omaishoidon tuen saajia tuli 413, ja tämän vuoden arvio on noin 430.

Asiakas voi täyttää OmaSavossa esimerkiksi iäkkäiden palvelujen hakemuksen, jolla voi hakea omaishoidon tukea ja kuljetuspalvelua. Hakemus siirtyy OmaSavosta suoraan ammattilaisen käsittelyyn.

Kun päätös on tehty, asiakas voi lukea sen OmaKannasta ja Suomi.fi-viestit-palvelusta. Jos asiakas ei ole ottanut Suomi.fi-viestejä käyttöön, hän saa päätöksen paperipostilla.

Ikäkeskuksen neuvontaan tulee kuukausittain keskimäärin 1 300–1 400 yhteydenottoa, joista 75 prosenttia on puhelinsoittoja.

title: Tanzanian Court Convicts Opposition Leader of Incitement
content:
Tanzania’s High Court on November 6 convicted Tundu Lissu, the leader of Tanzania’s main opposition party, Chama Cha Demokrasia Na Maendeleo (the ‘Party of Democracy and Development’, or CHADEMA), of incitement, sentencing him to four years in prison. The judges acquitted him of treason, a charge that carries the death penalty.

Authorities accused him of having planned to instigate the public to obstruct the October 2025 elections, based on remarks he made at an April 3, 2025, rally in Dar es Salaam. CHADEMA had been calling for the government to undertake “fundamental electoral reforms” as part of its campaign, “No Reforms, No Elections.” Prior to his conviction, Lissu had been imprisoned without bail since his April 9, 2025 arrest.

The proceedings against Lissu raised serious human rights concerns. His trial faced repeated delays, and he represented himself after saying the authorities had denied him private access to his lawyers.

title: EU accuses TikTok of designing algorithm that creates ‘rabbit holes’
content:
The European Commission has accused TikTok of violating its online platforms rules for having designed algorithms that lead users down so-called rabbit holes.

The preliminary findings announced Friday mark the first time the Commission has focused on a social media platform’s recommender systems as a breach of its powerful Digital Services Act, under which it can issue fines up to 6% of a company’s annual global revenue.

“This is the first time that we are really tackling head-on the engagement-based recommender system model,” said one Commission official, who was granted speaking anonymity to speak freely.

This is the fifth case of the EU executive accusing TikTok of breaching EU rules, even though it has issued no fines against the Chinese-owned platform.

In Friday’s announcement, the Commission says the company didn’t adequately consider the risk of sending users down “rabbit holes” through a “continuous stream of personalised videos, even when those are related to mental health struggles and body image.”

The investigation focused on mental health impacts because “the evidence was strongest,” when asked about how these rabbit holes contribute to radicalization, said another official.

title: In Conversation with Natalie Bennett, England and Wales
content:
Natalie Bennett, Baroness Bennett of Manor Castle, is UK Green politician and former journalist. She led the Green Party of England and Wales from 2012 to 2016 and has been a member of the UK House of Lords since 2019. Before entering politics, she was editor of the Guardian Weekly from 2007 to 2012. She also lived in Thailand for five years, where she volunteered with the National Commission on Women’s Affairs. 

In this interview, Natalie Bennet reflects on her journey from journalism to Green politics, the lessons behind the party’s electoral breakthroughs, and the role of European cooperation. She explores how Greens can gain political power without losing their movement roots, and why the future of Green politics depends on connecting ecological limits with public health, economic justice, and social wellbeing. 

Can you please introduce yourself?

title: Why Europe is building both a digital euro and a new mobile payment network
content:
Sending money from your phone seems simple: just choose a contact, enter an amount, and press confirm. But behind these apparently simple actions lie national payment systems that are not always interoperable.

In Europe, the Madrid-based European Network for Payments (ENP) has been established to link five mobile payment solutions operating in 13 European countries: Bizum (Spain), Bancomat (Italy), SIBS-MB WAY (Portugal), Vipps MobilePay (Norway, Denmark, Sweden and Finland) and EPI/Wero (Germany, Belgium, France, the Netherlands, Luxembourg and Austria).

The combined infrastructure of these organisations covers more than 70% of the population of the EU and Norway, serving a total of around 130 million active users.

The ENP’s rollout will be gradual, beginning with payment between individuals before progressing to online shopping and brick-and-mortar businesses.

But as the EU gets ready to launch the digital euro over the next few years, the question that will spring to mind for many is: Why bother?

Leer más: Why the EU economy should embrace digital currencies to become less dependent on the US

title: The Cop31 climate summit is betting on electrification – but still needs a plan to ditch fossil fuels
content:
The latest UN climate summit, Cop31, will get underway in Antalya, Turkey, on November 9. One of its key objectives is to boost electrification across the global economy – replacing petrol and diesel vehicles, gas boilers and some industrial processes that burn fossil fuels with electric alternatives.

The summit’s host, Turkey, has set a target of 35% of energy demand being met by electricity by 2035, up from around 20% today. Announcing the “35-by-35” pledge, Cop31 president Murat Kurum described it as “one of the defining features” of Turkey’s presidency, highlighting the risks of continued dependence on imported fossil fuels.

Without doubt, electrification is essential to curtailing greenhouse gas emissions, and is already gathering pace. The International Energy Agency (IEA) has declared we are living in the “age of electricity”, and if stated policy pledges hold, global electrification rates will hit 31% by 2050. The Cop31’s focus on electrification hopes to build upon and accelerate this existing trend.

title: ”Lopettakaa sodat. Lopettakaa naisten, tyttöjen ja kaikkien siviilien tappaminen.” – UN Womenin apulaispääjohtaja Nyaradzayi Gumbonzvandan puhe YK:n pääsihteerin Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuusraportin julkistamistilaisuudessa
content:
Ennen kuin aloitan, haluan kunnioittaa sodissa henkensä menettäneiden muistoa. Niiden naisten, miesten, tyttöjen ja poikien muistoa, joilta riistettiin tulevaisuus. Ja omien kollegoidemme muistoa – niiden, jotka menettivät henkensä yrittäessään pelastaa muita.

Joka päivä sota ja väkivalta avautuvat silmiemme edessä.

Puhelimissamme. Televisioruuduillamme. Loputtomana kuvavirtana tuhoutuneista kodeista, surevista äideistä, haavoittuneista lapsista ja perheistä, jotka pakenevat henkensä edestä.

Me näemme kaiken tämän. Emmekä silti näe koko kuvaa.

Tänään julkaistava YK:n pääsihteerin Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuus -raportti tuo näiden kuvien rinnalle tutkittua tietoa ja pakottaa meidät kohtaamaan järkyttävän todellisuuden:

Sodista on tulossa yhä tappavampia naisille ja tytöille. Ja maailma antaa sen tapahtua.

Tällä hetkellä yli 750 miljoonaa naista ja tyttöä elää alle 50 kilometrin päässä aktiivisesta konfliktialueesta. Heille sota ei ole jotakin, jonka ohi voi vain selata puhelimellaan. Sota on heidän kotiovellaan.

Sota seuraa naisia synnytysosastoille. Koululuokkiin. Keittiöihin. Paikkoihin, joissa perheiden pitäisi voida olla turvassa.

title: Tanzania: Conviction and sentencing of opposition leader Tundu Lissu a travesty of justice
content:
Reacting to Friday’s conviction of Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu and his sentence of four years’ imprisonment for incitement, after he was acquitted of treason, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa, Tigere Chagutah, said:

“Tundu Lissu should never have been arrested, let alone prosecuted and convicted. Today’s verdict and four-year prison sentence are the culmination of a deeply flawed process that was unjust from the moment of his arrest. He has already spent 577 days in arbitrary detention solely for the peaceful exercise of his human rights.
