title: Ulkomailla haettavien passi- ja henkilökorttihakemusten käsittelyyn esitetään muutoksia
content:
Ulkomailla haettavien passien ja henkilökorttien myöntämistä koskeva päätöksenteko esitetään siirrettäväksi Suomen edustustoilta ulkoministeriölle. Valtioneuvosto antoi eduskunnalle asiaa koskevan esityksen 5.11.2026. Lakimuutosten on tarkoitus tulla voimaan syksyllä 2027.

Esityksen mukaan ulkomailla oleskelevien Suomen kansalaisten passi- ja henkilökorttihakemuksia koskeva päätöksenteko keskitettäisiin Suomen edustustoilta ulkoministeriölle.

Suomen edustustot vastaanottaisivat jatkossakin passi- ja henkilökorttihakemuksia ulkomailla nykyiseen tapaan. Passi- ja henkilökorttitehtäviä voisivat hoitaa myös Suomen edustustoon työsuhteessa olevat henkilöt. Heidän kelpoisuudestaan, tehtävistään ja rikosoikeudellisesta virkavastuustaan säädettäisiin laissa.

Passilakiin ja henkilökorttilakiin lisättäisiin säännökset siitä, että Suomen edustustoissa passia varten jätettyjä sormenjälkiä voitaisiin hyödyntää henkilökortin hakemiseen ja päinvastoin.

Lisäksi henkilökorttilakia muutettaisiin siten, että alaikäisen henkilökorttia voisi hakea myös ulkomailla.

Passi- ja henkilökorttilainsäädännön Suomen kunniakonsulaatteja koskevat säännökset ajantasaistettaisiin ja selkeytettäisiin.

title: In the UK, Face Sitting Porn Might Land You in Jail
content:
“I adore breath play. I love being strangled, suffocated and drowned, and I love strangling and suffocating others. Waterboarding: that’s my favourite,” Melissa Todd, a UK-based writer and sex worker, told me. “Many women do: it really isn’t only horrid men forcing us to do these dreadful depraved acts. Interrupting oxygen supply produces the most intense sensation of euphoria. I enjoy it in my private life, and I offer it in sessions too.” 

Starting tomorrow, she and anyone else in the UK distributing or possessing this type of content, even if it’s just recorded in the privacy of their homes and not for sale on a porn site, could face up to five years in prison. The maximum penalty for possession is “two years’ imprisonment for pornography that depicts strangulation or suffocation, or penetrative sexual activity between certain relatives,” according to the law, and “three years’ imprisonment for pornography depicting sexual activity involving a person who is, or is pretending to be, under 16,” with five years as the maximum penalty for publication of all of the above.

title: Hong Kong: Joshua Wong Gets Nearly 10 More Years in Prison
content:
(Tokyo) – The Hong Kong High Court on November 5, 2026, sentenced Joshua Wong, a well-known democracy activist, to 10 years in prison on baseless national security charges, Human Rights Watch said today. Two months of the sentence will run concurrently with his current national security sentence. Wong has been in custody since November 2020, when he was 24, and faces imprisonment until late 2036, when he will be 40.

The Hong Kong government should immediately and unconditionally release Wong. Foreign governments should denounce the sentences against him and other wrongfully detained pro-democracy activists and impose targeted sanctions on officials responsible for Hong Kong’s growing repression.

“The harsh sentence on baseless charges against Joshua Wong is cruel and unjust,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Young people promoting social change are an asset for any vibrant society, but the Hong Kong government puts them behind bars.”

title: Hackers Steal Estimated 118 Million Euros in Cyberattack on French Bank
content:
French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa suffered a sophisticated cyberattack that allegedly siphoned an estimated 118 million euros ($132.44 million) from its corporate accounts, though the institution stated that client assets were untouched.

In a Wednesday public statement and a subsequent update, the bank explained that hackers infiltrated its systems through a third-party service provider's platform. The attackers bypassed client accounts entirely, using Crédit Mutuel Arkéa’s proprietary accounts to transfer funds to other banks. The stolen money was then potentially converted into cryptocurrency on specialized platforms, the bank said.

Addressing media reports that 118 million euros were stolen, the bank did not confirm the exact figure but validated the "order of magnitude."

title: EU budget battle paralyzes Brussels on AI chips, the Arctic and agriculture
content:
BRUSSELS — Europe’s push to accelerate AI chip production and plan to strengthen its Arctic presence are among the key EU policy files caught in the logjam of Brussels’ seven-year budget standoff.

European policymakers say they can’t move forward on their files without sufficient visibility on proposals linked to EU funding, as the negotiating impasse over the size of the EU’s 2028-2034 budget means financial allocations after next year are unknown.

“There’s an increase in sectoral legislation with objectives that require multiannual budgetary commitments,” said a person involved in talks on the EU budget, who was granted anonymity to discuss closed-door negotiations. “But the budget talks are disconnected from the policy discussions.”

EU governments are racing to find a deal among themselves over the total size of the money pot by the end of the year. The so-called frugal countries pushing for major budget cuts — Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Sweden, Denmark and Finland — have publicly said that a proposal by the Irish presidency of the Council of the EU envisioning €159 billion cuts doesn’t go far enough.

title: Apple iPad mini A20 Pro review: the best small tablet but with a big price
content:
All-round upgrades fit a bigger OLED screen in a smaller and lighter body with water resistance for first time

The new iPad mini takes Apple’s fan-favourite tiny tablet and upgrades just about everything about it, including giving it a new OLED screen, serious performance, speakers embedded into the display and even water resistance, all with a big new price tag.

The eighth-generation iPad mini costs from £699 (€749/$699/A$1,099), which is £200 or equivalent more than the original price of its predecessor as RAMageddon continues to bite. That makes it uncomfortably expensive, costing £270 more than the base model iPad (A16) and only £50 cheaper than the bigger 11in iPad Air M4.

title: Not too small to matter
content:
Big states cannot cover it all. Smaller European states are stepping in, creating influence through niche politics. Ultimately, the argument that smaller states need to identify WPS areas where they can bring real added value has the potential to create influence based on outside-the-box thinking.

The Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda is often discussed through the lens of major European powers, such as the United Kingdom, France and Germany. And although smaller European states, especially the Nordic countries, are recognised as crucial WPS actors, the contributions of other countries, such as Austria, Ireland and Czechia, remain comparatively under the radar. Sustaining the WPS agenda requires stronger alliances and broader coalitions. It is therefore worth examining what smaller states can contribute when using their niche. The relevance lies not simply in filling gaps left by larger powers, but in how smaller states can use their specific expertise to foster impactful WPS practices.

title: What makes music truly ‘Russian’? The forgotten debate between Tchaikovsky and his star pupil
content:
What makes a piece of music Russian? A folk tune, a church melody, or simply the fact that the composer was born in Russia? For 19th-century composer Sergei Taneyev (1856-1915), the answer was complicated. He wanted Russian composers to develop a musical voice of their own. But he believed they could do so by learning from composers elsewhere in Europe.

By the time Taneyev began his career, the world of classical music in Russia was expanding. Musical life, which had previously been centred on the imperial court and aristocratic families, increasingly came to include public concerts and new institutions for training professional musicians. Conservatoires opened in St Petersburg in 1862 and in Moscow in 1866, where teaching methods developed in various European countries were employed.

title: SLS käynnistää uusia tukimuotoja tutkimukseen, kirjallisuuteen, kulttuuriperinnön digitointiin ja humanististen tieteiden vahvistamiseen
content:
Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland (SLS) avaa haettavaksi useita uusia tukimuotoja vuodesta 2027 alkaen. Tohtorin tutkinnon suorittaneille tutkijoille suunnattujen työpaikkojen lisäksi hakuun tulee uusia tukimuotoja kirjallisuuden edistämiseen ja kulttuuriperinnön digitointiin. SLS käynnistää myös kokonaan uuden avustusmuodon hankkeille, joiden tavoitteena on vahvistaa humanististen tieteiden asemaa yhteiskunnassa.

Kirjallisuustuet

SLS avaa haettavaksi kaksi uutta kirjallisuutta edistävää avustusta:

Tuotantotuki ammattimaisille kustantajille laadukkaan ja monipuolisen kirjallisuustarjonnan ylläpitämiseksi sekä ruotsinkielisen kirjallisuuden monimuotoisuuden edistämiseksi Suomessa. Tukea voi käyttää esimerkiksi toimitustyöhön, graafiseen suunnitteluun, painatuskustannuksiin sekä e-kirjojen ja äänikirjojen tuotantoon.

Tuki kirjallisuutta edistäviin hankkeisiin, kuten kirjallisuusaiheisten videoiden tuotantoon, paikallisiin kirjallisuusfestivaaleihin ja kirjamessuihin sekä kirjallisuuteen ja lukemiseen liittyviin markkinointikampanjoihin. Tukea voivat hakea Suomessa toimivat tapahtumien järjestäjät.

title: UK Expands Human Rights Sanctions Regime
content:
The UK has significantly expanded its Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime, allowing the government, for the first time, to impose targeted sanctions on individuals and entities involved in war crimes. The new powers were approved by parliament yesterday.

The previous framework, adopted in 2020, did not allow for such sanctions, providing, instead, for targeted sanctions only for certain serious human rights violations of the right to life, freedom from torture, and freedom from slavery and forced labor. Under the new rules, the government can also target those responsible for serious violations of international humanitarian law, obstruction of humanitarian assistance, and violations of the right to liberty and security of person.

This is an important step that means the UK can impose consequences for atrocities committed around the world. Although Foreign Secretary, Ed Miliband, announced the change in September while laying out measures to address Israel’s unlawful settlement expansion in the West Bank, the powers can also be used against those responsible for war crimes anywhere.
snippet: The UK has significantly expanded its Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime, allowing the government, for the first time, to impose targeted sanctions on individuals and entities involved in war

title: Russia denies involvement in fridge hacks across Europe
content:
A spokesperson for the Kremlin denied on Thursday that Russia had any involvement in the cyberattacks affecting supermarket refrigerators, calling the allegations “absurd.”

Dmitry Peskov said accusations of Russian involvement in the attacks are “unfounded,” according to reports in Russian media. These allegations are “becoming a persistent trend in European countries,” he added.

Supermarket refrigerators have been hacked in multiple European countries over the past few weeks, forcing retailers to throw away thawing fresh and frozen food. The attacks also hit French blood banks, though the country’s blood collection service said its supplies were not affected.

While pro-Russian hacker groups claimed the attacks on Wednesday, it is notoriously difficult to attribute a cyberattack to a specific actor definitively, and those groups quickly deleted the claims, according to the BBC.

title: Elon Musk’s nearly half a billion dollars in midterms spending was a flop
content:
The tech billionaire set spending record as he poured $446m into campaigns for failed Republican candidates

Elon Musk set a record for election spending this year after pouring nearly half a billion dollars into backing Republicans in the US midterm elections. It turned out to be a poor investment.

The SpaceX and Tesla CEO contributed at least $446m to Republican-aligned Super Pacs and groups over the course of the elections, specifically targeting several key Senate races in an effort to help the Trump administration retain Republican control of Congress. He outdid his own 2024 spending of nearly $290m. Yet as Democrats swept to power across the country on Tuesday night, it became clear that Musk would get nearly nothing in return for his hundreds of millions in spending.

title: The Binance hack exploited familiar weaknesses – all organisations should learn from it
content:
Hackers have stolen around US$6.3 billion (£4.7 billion) from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance, most of which was taken in under an hour. According to Binance, the attack exploited systems and individuals with the authority to carry out transactions involving such large sums.

Such vulnerabilities exist everywhere; statistics show that people and the systems they directly use, including their personal computers, remain a top target for cybercriminals. All organisations could therefore learn lessons from this attack.

The Binance theft took place on the evening of October 29, 2026. The Binance attack netted four times the amount stolen in the previous biggest cryptocurrency theft, on the Bybit exchange in February 2025.

Private keys, used to authorise spending or withdrawal from crypto-wallets, are a known vulnerability. But Binance found no evidence these were leaked. An initial statement from the exchange pointed to a compromised laptop belonging to an engineer. This gave the attacker access to the internal system that processes withdrawal requests.

title: Young men and Latino voters helped drive the Democrats’ blue wave. Why did they abandon Trump?
content:
The young men and Hispanic and Latino voters who helped propel Donald Trump to his presidential victory in 2024 swung sharply towards the Democrats in the midterm elections, contributing to the historic defeat for Republicans.

Charles Hunt, an associate professor of political science at Boise State University in Idaho, tells The Conversation Weekly podcast that the results suggest weakened support for Trump and his MAGA movement among these key groups of voters.

Hispanic and Latino voters “swung heavily towards Trump in 2024”, Hunt says. But midterm results in Florida, Texas and elsewhere “are showing these voters just slingshotting completely in the other direction,” he explains, citing early exit polls and analysis by The New York Times.

Not just back towards where they were in, say, 2018 or 2020 in terms of support for Democrats, but past that – being more supportive of folks like James Talarico in Texas than they have been of any Democrat in the last 20 years.

That’s really, really significant, especially since that’s a growing part of the electorate.

title: Republicans Learn X Is the Echo Chamber

There's a BlazeTV YouTube video whose thumbnail shows the presenter with his arms around Anakin Skywalker and a gender-flipped Draco Malfoy called Malfoid. “Total Chud Victory?” It says. The video's title: “Young Right is Reclaiming Culture and Liberals Are Mad About it.”

BlazeTV posted the video on November 2, the day before Democrats swept the midterms and started a political realignment in America so overwhelming that Republicans lost control of all the most powerful state positions in Texas.

The video is a profound misreading of the political and cultural moment. It reminded me of stories of the Bolsheviks seizing the Winter Palace to discover tarot card playing courtiers who had no idea a revolution was happening in the streets.

The American version was watching defense contractor Palmer Lucky dress up like Harry Potter on Halloween while standing next to his Malfoid wife. And it was Elon Musk — who spent roughly half a billion on the election only to see his chosen candidates fail — posting an AI generated picture of Anakin Skywalker sitting at the head of a happy fascist Star Wars family two days before the midterms.

title: ‘Stop using US tech’: EU lawmaker says Starlink service cutoff led to deaths
content:
“Stop using U.S. tech. That’s my message,” Finnish EPP lawmaker Aura Salla declared Thursday at the European Pulse Seminar.

In an interview with POLITICO, Salla argued that last month’s speed cap on the SpaceX military Starshield service in Ukraine was “yet another example of a kill switch,” which in this case led directly to battlefield deaths.

“We are losing lives in Ukraine. It’s about our defense, because defense is technology.”

Salla issued her stark warning as a pushback against Brussels’ growing focus on AI adoption over building frontier models in Europe. In her Sept. 16 State of the Union address, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said: “We do not need to be the ones who develop the frontier technology to be the ones who draw the greatest value from it.”

Salla argued that Europe needs frontier models to have “any room in these negotiations,” over the direct of artificial development and safety. Leading French frontier lab Mistral has likewise warned that Europe will be shut out from shaping AI without a player leading development of the most advance models.

Kate Brennan, who leads AI and corporate power policy at the AI Now Institute, told TechCrunch that Lehane’s rhetoric marks a notable shift from OpenAI’s policy agenda last year, which focused on accelerating AI development, reducing regulatory barriers, and expanding infrastructure.

title: Europe: Get Satellites or Get Throttled
content:
European powers must urgently break Elon Musk’s near-monopoly over military communications. It won’t be easy. It won’t be cheap. It won’t happen fast. But it’s necessary to ensure no one man can repeat the trillionaire’s treatment of Ukraine in early October, when he throttled Ukraine’s access to the Starlink and Starshield satellite systems now central to its military operations.

Starlink is a commercial satellite communications service, with Starshield a more capable military version. Both belong to Musk’s SpaceX. Ukraine — and many other Western powers, for that matter — relies on them for an array of vital military functions. They connect troops to their headquarters and drones to their operators.

Overnight and without warning in mid-October, thousands of satellite terminals failed in Ukraine. Operators discovered that SpaceX had imposed a speed limit of approximately 160 kmh (100 mph) or slower. Above that speed, a drone couldn’t connect to its operator. Many of the faster drones, including interceptor drones that Ukraine uses to defeat Russia’s own attack drones, couldn’t function.

content:
A collection of essays by five international experts reflects on how Ukraine’s relationships with countries in Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Middle East have evolved since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.

CMI has published five short essays by journalists, academics and specialists in international relations and diplomacy that consider how external perceptions of Ukraine have shifted over the past four years. The authors trace some of Ukraine’s regional engagement strategies, and present opportunities and challenges for cooperation in the future.

The collection is a byproduct of CMI’s work in supporting relationships and mutual understanding between Ukrainian actors and international counterparts. According to Edward Marques, Head of CMI’s Eurasia Programme, the contributions “reflect the diversity of perspectives that now shape international discussions about Ukraine and, more broadly, about the future of international order.”

title: Culture gains a stronger name and place in the European Parliament’s Horizon Europe compromise
content:
Culture Action Europe is proud to be part of the Name Place Fund coalition, which brings together culture and research organisations advocating for stronger support for culture in Horizon Europe and the European Competitiveness Fund. The coalition welcomes the cross-party compromise text on Horizon Europe 2028-2034 negotiated in the European Parliament. 

It was prepared by rapporteurs Christian Ehler (EPP) and René Repasi (S&D) together with the shadow rapporteurs. The compromise is scheduled for a vote in Parliament’s Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE) Committee on 10 November. This text will be the starting point for the Parliament’s negotiations with the Commission and the Council. 

After long negotiations, culture, creativity and artistic research finally have a more prominent place in the future EU research and innovation programme, signalling an important shift in how the role of arts and culture in research and innovation is understood.

title: US midterms delivered a blow to tech’s AI ambitions
content:
There’s no question the US midterms elections delivered a blow to Donald Trump. The Democrats took not just the House and Senate back from the Republicans, but won a wave of governor’s races across the country — including in states it would’ve previously been hard to imagine a Democrat winning.

But it wasn’t just Trump who lost. The tech industry and its ambitions to cover the country in hyperscale data centers to power generative AI were potentially even bigger losers than the orange man himself.

It didn’t matter that Elon Musk shelled out over $400 million to try to save Republicans as polling increasingly suggested a wipeout was coming, especially in his chosen home of Texas, or that crypto and AI companies deployed millions more on races across the country. An NBC News exit poll still found 56% of voters said AI and data centers were “crucial or a major factor” in their vote for Congress. And it showed in the results.

title: Launch of European.Social: the movement for the European open social web
content:
Today, November 4, the European.Social movement was officially launched in Berlin with a celebratory event at the location of Wikimedia Deutschland. The movement takes on a legal form in the European Social Association e.V., which was also established today. The association will coordinate the movement for open, decentralised and interoperable social media in Europe. More than 150 organisations and almost 700 individuals support the initiative, including PublicSpaces.

European.Social began as a shared manifesto, launched on 5 June 2026 at the PublicSpaces Conference with 12 founding signatories – including PublicSpaces. Since then, the movement has grown with 40 builders, 14 communities, 86 organisations and 676 individuals. Together, they are building open social infrastructure for Europe from a set of shared values and principles like democracy, digital autonomy and open source.

title: Burning questions about burning trash
content: Depending on where you live, your waste can take several routes. About half of the waste in the EU gets recycled or composted, the rest ends up either in a landfill or a giant furnace. Burning waste in specialised plants can transform that waste into energy – something that Europe constantly needs more of. Sounds like a win-win? Not so fast. Though incinerating waste reduces the amount sent to landfills and the resulting methane emissions, burning generates ashes, metals, and large quantities of CO₂. “Incinerators are among the most carbon-intensive energy sources in some countries,” Janek Vähk, a policy manager at Zero Waste Europe, told us. “Because these plants are less efficient in energy generation, the greenhouse gas emissions per unit of electricity are almost double those of fossil gas power.” Modern waste-to-energy plants, such as Vienna's colourful Spittelau plant, can limit negative environmental impacts with advanced filtering systems. title: Vermont Was Supposed to Get an Audit of Its Lake Champlain Cleanup. It Never Happened.
content:
This summer, Vermont’s Clean Water Board celebrated a milestone: Over the past decade, the state has invested nearly a billion dollars to clean up its polluted streams, rivers and lakes. The vast majority of that money has gone toward Lake Champlain.

“I think that’s something to be extremely proud of,” said Douglas Farnham, the board’s chair.

Vermont was supposed to get an independent evaluation of what it has gotten for all that money. But that study was never done.

A decade ago, Vermont lawmakers mandated that the board submit an audit from an outside environmental consultant to determine whether the projects the state had invested in to improve water quality were working. The audit also was meant to examine whether the state’s agriculture and natural resource agencies are doing enough to enforce water quality regulations on farms, which are the biggest source of phosphorus in Lake Champlain.

Seven Days and ProPublica have teamed up to investigate the cleanup of Lake Champlain. Have you been affected by this issue? We’d like to hear from you.

title: The 2027 Mark Palmer Prize: Call for Nominations
content:
Freedom House is now accepting nominations for the 2027 Mark Palmer Prize, inviting individuals and organizations around the world to put forward candidates whose work exemplifies the important role of diplomacy in supporting democratic movements and defending fundamental freedoms.

The award takes its name from the late Mark Palmer, a longtime Freedom House trustee and US ambassador to Hungary from 1986 to 1990. In 1989, as the Cold War was coming to a close, Palmer boldly joined civil society and the Hungarian democratic opposition to support the country’s transition to democracy.
 
The Mark Palmer Prize has been awarded to diplomats and international civil servants from around the world, including Georgia, Peru, the Czech Republic, Lithuania, Mongolia, Sweden, Canada, Uruguay, and the United States. The prize is made possible through the generosity of the Mark and Sushma Palmer Legacy Fund, established by Dr. Sushma Palmer in loving memory of her late husband and former Freedom House trustee and vice chairman Ambassador Mark Palmer.
